subject: MSA + Order Form: Term, Renewal & Termination Redlines

Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: MSA + Order Form: Term, Renewal & Termination Redlines

Hi Sara,

Thanks for sending the draft MSA and the Order Form. Attached are our redlines for both documents. I highlighted the sections we think will need the most attention during legal review — primarily term, renewal, and termination. High-level asks below so legal can triage quickly: 

- Auto-renew: Proposed language is one 12-month renewal term unless either party provides notice X days prior. We redlined to 60 days notice to avoid surprise renewals for our customers.
- Notice windows: We flagged several inconsistent notice periods across the MSA and Order Form; suggested harmonizing to 60 days for renewals and 30 days for other notices.
- Termination for convenience: We propose mutual termination for convenience with a 60-day notice and a limited wind-down payment (pro-rated committed fees or a capped fee equivalent to 3 months of committed spend). This protects both parties and avoids sudden capacity write-downs.

Can you confirm whether Acme is able to accept the 60-day renewal notice and the mutual termination-for-convenience approach? If you have firm constraints (e.g., 30 days notice only), call that out and we can escalate to our Contracts team.

Attachments: 20260210-MSA-redline.pdf (application/pdf), OrderForm_v2_redline.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the quick turn. A few quick notes from our side: 

- Auto-renew: Acme standard is 30 days notice prior to renewal for SaaS agreements. We can try to stretch to 45 days but 60 would be difficult operationally for our procurement calendar.
- Termination for convenience: Our procurement prefers termination for convenience to be on the customer side only (i.e., Acme can terminate for convenience with 30 days notice and pay for the termination wind-down as set out). We rarely accept mutual termination for convenience because of vendor capacity planning.
- Notice windows: Agree the documents have inconsistent notice periods; we will accept harmonizing them but prefer 30 days for most notices and 30 for renewals.

Please see attached with our redline (OrderForm_v2_Acme_redline.docx). If Redwood's legal team can provide alternative language that still meets the needs above (particularly the single-sided termination-for-convenience), please share.

Best,
Sara Polk
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Payments, Inc.
sara.polk@acmepayments.com

Marissa / Laura —

Thanks for the context and for forwarding Acme's positions. Below are our legal team's recommended positions and a proposed compromise clause set you can present to Acme for quick resolution. High-level: we should avoid unilateral termination-for-convenience (it exposes us to sudden lost committed capacity). We can offer a compromise but need contractual protection.

Summary of recommended positions:
1) Auto-renew notice window: Recommend 60 days prior written notice to avoid unintended renewals. If Acme cannot accept 60 days, offer 45 days as a commercial compromise but only if Acme agrees to the wind-down payment on termination-for-convenience.

2) Termination for convenience: Recommend mutual termination for convenience with 60 days' notice. If Acme insists on single-sided termination for convenience, allow it only with a defined wind-down payment equal to the greater of (i) pro-rated fees for 30 days of committed services, or (ii) a capped termination fee equal to three (3) months of the then-current committed monthly fees. This ensures cost recovery for any pre-allocated capacity and a predictable cap.

Suggested clause language (clean):
"Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon sixty (60) days prior written notice to the other party. In the event of termination for convenience by Customer, Customer shall pay Provider for all Services performed through the effective date of termination and a wind-down fee equal to the greater of (i) pro-rated fees for thirty (30) days of committed services, or (ii) a capped fee equal to three (3) months of the then-current committed monthly fees. The wind-down fee shall be the sole remedy for Provider for any such termination for convenience."

If Acme will not accept mutual termination-for-convenience but will accept our capped wind-down fee, then pass the 45-day compromise on renewal notice; otherwise hold firm on 60 days. Also confirm that warranty/indemnity and SLA exit obligations survive termination for the duration necessary to preserve customer data for 30 days.

If you want, I can prepare a tracked-change MSA with the above language and a short explanation memo for Acme procurement. Otherwise, propose the 45-day/ wind-down payment compromise to speed closure.

Rishi Malhotra
